stand: The US-Israel war on Iran, launched 28 Feb, is in its eighth month. Trump rules out new strikes before the 3 Nov midterms, citing 'productive discussions' with Tehran, though the blockade stays in place; US media report the Pentagon is readying plans to resume major combat afterwards. Iran's Atomic Energy Organization refuses to abandon enrichment or hand over its stockpile. Putin has pledged to help end the war. A UN-mandated mission says the US may have committed war crimes at Minab. Qatar says talks continue; Iraq has devalued its dinar.

figures.label: Strait of Hormuz daily oil exports

claims.text: The US withdrew all its bomber aircraft from RAF Fairford after a security incident.
claims.by: Says: Pentagon spokesperson, confirmed to CBS News Denies: —

claims.text: The alleged RAF Fairford plot involved a suspected complex drone attack; a further suspect, a 22-year-old man, was arrested in London.
claims.by: Says: Two US officials, speaking anonymously, to Reuters; British police confirm new London arrest Denies: Iran denies any involvement

claims.text: The war has sharply cut Strait of Hormuz oil exports, driving up global fuel prices.
claims.by: Says: Al Jazeera, citing AAA price data Denies: —

claims.text: Combined crude volumes from the Gulf excluding Iran, plus Saudi and UAE output, are now around pre-conflict levels at roughly 18.5 million bpd, up from the 18.3 million bpd late-September figure.
claims.by: Says: Kpler data, cited by Matt Wright, Kpler lead freight analyst

claims.text: Global oil stockpiles are now scarily thin, with most commercial inventories not practically available.
claims.by: Says: Saudi Aramco chief executive Amin Nasser Denies: —

claims.text: Iran's foreign minister says only negotiations, not military moves, can end the war.
claims.by: Says: Iranian FM Abbas Araghchi Denies: —

claims.text: Israeli and US strikes hit more than 40 ballistic missile, nearly 20 cruise missile and over 20 drone industry sites, severely damaging Iran's production base.
claims.by: Says: Iranian officials say production and improvement continue; War on the Rocks analyst assessment finds severe damage to production sites Denies: US and Israeli officials say Iran can no longer produce missiles and drones

claims.text: Katz's West Bank plan envisages a short, powerful offensive with ground, air and special forces if Palestinian Authority forces and Tanzim arm against settlers or troops.
claims.by: Says: Defence Minister Israel Katz, per Times of Israel, cited by TASS

claims.text: The UN Secretary-General has called for an end to the Iran war and restoration of navigational rights.
claims.by: Says: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres Denies: —

claims.text: Trump says he was talking about gasoline prices, not about losing Los Angeles or San Diego, blaming 'fake and artificial news' for the furore over his remarks.
claims.by: Says: President Donald Trump, on Truth Social Denies: —

claims.text: Vance says Iran must cut its 60%-enriched uranium stockpile, not just promise future drawdowns, to end the war; Washington is talking to Iran's president and foreign minister but is unsure how much power they actually hold.
claims.by: Says: US Vice President JD Vance, to Reuters Denies: —

claims.text: Joint US-Israeli strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei at the start of the war.
claims.by: Says: US Vice President JD Vance, to Reuters

claims.text: Trump says no one knows who is running Iran; Iran's foreign ministry denies, blaming contradictory US messaging.
claims.by: Says: Trump says his biggest problem is no one knows who is running Iran Denies: Iran FM spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei says the problem is contradictory US positions

claims.text: Iran executed two more men, Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raisi, over January's protests, bringing the total executed to 34.
claims.by: Says: Iran's judiciary (Mizan News Agency), per Al-Monitor; tally per Iran Human Rights Organization

claims.text: The Philippines declared a national energy emergency over war-driven fuel disruption, warning supplies could run dry in 45 days.
claims.by: Says: Philippine Energy Secretary Sharon Garin, per Al Jazeera

claims.text: Iranian forces can periodically strike commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz but are largely unable to stop energy exports through the waterway.
claims.by: Says: US Vice President JD Vance, to Reuters Denies: —

claims.text: Iraq devalued its dinar from about 1,300 to 1,500 per dollar, as Hormuz-linked disruption widened the gap with the market rate.
claims.by: Says: Iraq's central bank Denies: —

claims.text: Iran's president says the country is in a state of full-scale war and is negotiating from that position to defend its people's rights.
claims.by: Says: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, per Fars news agency, cited by TASS Denies: —

claims.text: The war's shutdown of Strait of Hormuz trade halted global fertiliser shipments and spiked prices, squeezing African smallholder farmers.
claims.by: Says: NPR Denies: —

claims.text: The Pentagon has instructed US Central Command to prepare for 'imminent major combat operations' against Iran, with plans developed despite Trump's reported 'ambivalence', for use after the midterms if authorised.
claims.by: Says: Axios and Israeli officials, the Atlantic and the New York Times, cited by Al Jazeera Denies: —

claims.text: US national security officials are weighing resumed large-scale military operations against Iran, possibly including heavy bombing of energy, infrastructure and nuclear sites before the midterms.
claims.by: Says: NBC News and Axios, citing US officials

claims.text: Iran's foreign ministry says it has clearly and firmly set out its conditions for ending the war and will respond to US proposals through mediators.
claims.by: Says: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei

claims.text: Iran and Oman have agreed on safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz.
claims.by: Says: Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei

claims.text: Qatar says the US and Iran remain in indirect talks to end the war despite an apparent deadlock seven months in.
claims.by: Says: Qatari foreign ministry official Ibrahim al-Hashmi

claims.text: There have been nine attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month, half September's combined total for the strait and the Gulf.
claims.by: Says: UK Maritime Trade Operations

claims.text: Twelve crew members on a Panama-flagged tanker were injured in an attack by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz.
claims.by: Says: India's Ministry of External Affairs

claims.text: Washington is in control of the Strait of Hormuz and oil flows are close to normal levels.
claims.by: Says: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio

claims.text: Iran is taking part in the SCO's "Eurasia Antiterror 2026" counterterrorism exercise in Belarus with Russia, China, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
claims.by: Says: CIS Anti-Terrorism Center

claims.text: China has rebuffed Iranian requests to intervene more actively in Iran's war with the US and Israel.
claims.by: Says: Al-Monitor

claims.text: Global fertiliser prices largely dropped over the summer, including in Zambia, though some fertilisers remain expensive in Malawi, Tanzania and South Africa.
claims.by: Says: NPR

claims.text: Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton privately admitted the Iran war's effect on gas and diesel prices is Republicans' biggest problem before the midterms.
claims.by: Says: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, in audio leaked to Axios

claims.text: Trump now rules out attacking Iran before the 3 November midterms, reversing his Wednesday stance, and cites 'productive discussions' with Tehran while the blockade stays in place.
claims.by: Says: President Donald Trump, in a Truth Social post Denies: —

claims.text: Iran's Atomic Energy Organization says Tehran will not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its stockpile, rejecting Vance's demand for cuts.
claims.by: Says: Head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, per Iranian state media Denies: —

claims.text: Pezeshkian says Iran is engaged in dialogue but that the US attacks again every time they negotiate, and demands a 'final framework' to end the war.
claims.by: Says: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, per Iranian state media Denies: —

claims.text: Iran's President Pezeshkian says talks with Washington are 'meaningless' and accuses the US of trying to impose its policies unilaterally.
claims.by: Says: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, per Iranian state media Denies: —

claims.text: The Congressional Budget Office names the US-Israeli war on Iran 'Operation Epic Fury', reporting at least 81 US aircraft lost or damaged at a cost of between $1.9bn and $3.3bn as of 1 August.
claims.by: Says: Congressional Budget Office Denies: —

claims.text: Senator Chris Murphy says Hegseth is trying to hide the Iran war's costs and consequences from the American public by restricting his access to US bases.
claims.by: Says: Senator Chris Murphy, to reporters Denies: Pentagon official says the restriction was communicated in advance and applied evenly

claims.text: An Iranian drone strike on the US embassy in Riyadh caused far more extensive, multi-floor damage than Saudi Arabia initially disclosed, Murphy says.
claims.by: Says: Senator Chris Murphy, who visited the site Denies: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry initially described the damage as minor

claims.text: Iranian drone strikes early in the war halted LNG production at Qatar's Ras Laffan complex, eliminating 17% of Qatar's exports for an estimated three years.
claims.by: Says: Senator Chris Murphy, citing his visit to Ras Laffan Denies: —

claims.text: News reports have highlighted deteriorating conditions, food shortages and suicide attempts among USS Lincoln crew during its record deployment.
claims.by: Says: News reports, per Al Jazeera Denies: Pentagon chief Hegseth says media sought to portray the ship as a symbol of dysfunction or low morale

claims.text: Trump's former defense secretary Mark Esper says the Iran war could drag on well into 2027, or be handed to the next administration in 2029.
claims.by: Says: Former US Defense Secretary Mark Esper, to CNBC Denies: —

claims.text: A Pew Research Center poll found 65% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran war, against 33% approval.
claims.by: Says: Pew Research Center Denies: —

claims.text: The US deployment of 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines, including the USS Theodore Roosevelt strike group, has raised US troop numbers in the Middle East to 20,000, with hundreds of aircraft and at least three carrier strike groups.
claims.by: Says: Al Jazeera Denies: —

claims.text: Trump claims 22 million barrels of oil moved through the Strait of Hormuz overnight with none to or from Iran; CNBC could not verify the figure.
claims.by: Says: President Donald Trump Denies: —

claims.text: A Reuters/Ipsos poll found only 30% of Trump's 2024 supporters are enthusiastic about voting in the midterms, against 48% of Democratic voters; 13% of 2024 Trump voters are unsure who to back.
claims.by: Says: Reuters/Ipsos poll Denies: —

claims.text: A UN-mandated fact-finding mission concluded the US may have committed war crimes in the 28 February strikes on a school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd.
claims.by: Says: UN-mandated fact-finding mission, per Middle East Eye Denies: —

claims.text: Iran is pursuing national and international legal action over the Minab attack; local authorities reported 156 dead, independent sources citing the UN reported 157.
claims.by: Says: Iran's Deputy Minister for Human Rights Askar Jalalian, per IRNA; toll per Middle East Eye Denies: —

timeline.text: US and Israel launch war against Iran.
Joint US-Israeli opening strikes killed Iran's Supreme Leader Khamenei, Vance later reveals.
US resumes large-scale strikes on Iran, accusing Tehran of violating the Hormuz agreement.
Saudi Arabia and the US strike PMF targets in Iraq, killing at least 20.
Iran's foreign minister blames US and Israeli actions for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz.
Five British nationals arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of explosives and terror offences.
US-led coalition withdraws from Iraq; 90-day halt on paramilitary military activity begins.
Turkey announces handover of the Bashiqa-Zelikan camp near Mosul to the Iraqi government.
Senior Trump officials meet at Camp David on the Iran war and Houthi-Saudi conflict; G7 leaders agree to release diesel stockpiles.
Another tanker is struck in the Strait of Hormuz by an unknown projectile.
Pentagon confirms all US bombers withdrawn from RAF Fairford.
Trump blames Democrats and Ukraine's refinery strikes, not the Iran war, for rising US fuel prices.
UN chief Guterres calls for diplomacy and restoration of navigational rights, speaking in Islamabad.
Saudi Aramco chief Amin Nasser warns global oil stockpiles are scarily thin.
Iran executes Alireza Sepahi and Alireza Raisi over January protests.
Vance says Iran must meaningfully cut enrichment to end war; Trump rejected Tehran's latest proposal.
Congressional Budget Office reports at least 81 US aircraft lost or damaged in the war, costing up to $3.3bn.
Trump says Los Angeles and San Diego could be destroyed, calls it a small price to pay, and says the war is almost over.
Israel's defence minister Katz orders the army to prepare a full-scale offensive against the Palestinian Authority in the West Bank.
British police arrest a 22-year-old man in London in the RAF Fairford drone-plot investigation.
War on the Rocks assesses Israeli and US strikes hit 40+ missile, cruise and drone industry sites in Iran.
Katz details a short, powerful West Bank offensive plan if the PA and Tanzim arm against Israel.
Guterres praises Pakistan's role mediating between the US and Iran, speaking in Islamabad.
UK Maritime Trade Operations reports nine attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month, half September's total.
Panama-flagged tanker struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz, injuring 12 crew.
IRGC team arrives in Belarus for the SCO's Eurasia Antiterror 2026 drill, due to begin 9 Oct.
Iraq's central bank devalues the dinar from about 1,300 to 1,500 per dollar amid Hormuz-linked disruption.
Pezeshkian says Iran is fighting a full-scale war while still negotiating to defend Iranians' rights, speaking in Rabat.
Trump says he no longer wants a deal with Iran; US reportedly weighs resuming large-scale strikes before the midterms.
Iran's foreign ministry says it has set firm conditions to end the war and will respond to US proposals via mediators.
Iran and Oman agree on safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatar says US-Iran indirect talks continue despite deadlock.
Leaked audio shows Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton admitting Iran-war gas prices are hurting Republicans before the midterms.
Trump rules out attacking Iran before 3 Nov midterms, citing 'productive discussions' with Tehran.
Putin tells Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan that Russia will do everything to help end the war.
Pezeshkian says talks with Washington are 'meaningless' and accuses the US of unilateralism.
Senator Chris Murphy says the Pentagon blocked his access to Al Udeid base and is hiding the war's true costs.
USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after a record-length deployment supporting the war.
Esper says the Iran war could drag on well into 2027 or be handed to the next US administration.
Pew poll finds 65% of Americans disapprove of Trump's handling of the Iran war.
Reuters/Ipsos poll finds only 30% of Trump's 2024 supporters enthusiastic about voting in midterms, against 48% of Democrats.
Trump blames 'fake and artificial news' for the furore over his Los Angeles/San Diego remarks, says he meant gasoline prices.
Axios, the Atlantic and NYT report the Pentagon has ordered CENTCOM to prepare plans for major combat operations against Iran after the midterms.
Iran's deputy human rights minister says Iran is pursuing legal action over the Minab school attack, citing a UN-mandated mission's war-crimes finding.
US and Iran sign memorandum of understanding for a ceasefire including Lebanon.

headline: US Pentagon reportedly readies Iran strike plans for after midterms
